questions.question: Which is the internal energy reserve in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch**__.

• Starch is a **polysaccharide** that serves as a form of energy storage in plants.
 
• It is composed of numerous **glucose units** joined together by glycosidic bonds.
 
• Plants synthesize starch during photosynthesis and store it generally in plastids.
 
• Starch can be broken down into glucose molecules when the plant needs energy for growth and other metabolic activities.
 
• It is a **complex carbohydrate** that is insoluble in water, making it a good storage form of energy.

• Glucose is involved in cellular respiration to produce ATP.
 
 
 
• **Sucrose**
 
 
• It is a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose.
 
• Sucrose is commonly found in plants and is used for energy transport.

questions.question: If the mode of the following data is 7, then find the value of k.2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mode of the data = 7

Data = {2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13}

**Formula used:**

Mode = The value that appears most frequently in the data.

**Calculation:**

The frequency of each value:

2 appears 1 time

4 appears 1 time

6 appears 3 times

7 appears 3 times

5, 10, 9, and 13 each appear 1 time

2k + 1 appears 1 time

Since mode = 7, the frequency of 7 must be higher than any other number.

Currently, frequency of 7 = 3

Frequency of 6 = 3

To make 7 the mode, the frequency of 7 must increase. This means 2k + 1 = 7.

⇒ 2k + 1 = 7

⇒ 2k = 7 - 1

⇒ 2k = 6

⇒ k = 3

**∴ The value of k is 3.**

questions.question: The work done by a constant force of 5 Newton acting on a body is 5 joules. The displacement of the body in the direction of the applied force is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The work done by a force is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement**.
 
• Given the work done is 5 joules and the force applied is 5 Newtons.
 
• Rearranging the formula to find displacement: **Displacement = Work / Force**.
 
• Substituting the given values: **Displacement = 5 J / 5 N = 1 m**.
 
• Hence, the displacement in the direction of the applied force is **1 meter**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**

 
 
• This theorem states that the work done by the net force on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as Work = ΔK.E.
 
 
 
• **Units of Work**
 
 
• The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
 
• 1 joule is defined as the work done when a force of 1 Newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Types of Forces**
 
 
• Forces can be categorized into various types such as gravitational force, normal force, frictional force, and applied force.
 
• In this context, the force mentioned is an applied force of 5 Newtons acting on the body.

questions.question: The LCM of 24, 42, and 56 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 24, 42, 56

**Formula Used:**

LCM (Least Common Multiple) = The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.

**Calculation:**

Prime factorization:

24 = 2³ × 3¹

42 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 7¹

56 = 2³ × 7¹

LCM is found by taking the highest power of each prime number present in the factorization of each number.

LCM = 2³ × 3¹ × 7¹

LCM = 8 × 3 × 7

⇒ LCM = 168

**The LCM of 24, 42, and 56 is 168.**

questions.question: Magnification produced by a convex mirror for a given object of height 5 cm is 0.2. Here, the height of the image is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Magnification (m) produced by a mirror is given by the ratio of the height of the image (hᵢ) to the height of the object (hₒ).
 
• Mathematically, magnification (m) = hᵢ / hₒ.
 
• Given magnification (m) = 0.2 and height of the object (hₒ) = 5 cm.
 
• Substituting the values into the magnification formula: 0.2 = hᵢ / 5 cm.
 
• Solving for hᵢ, we get hᵢ = 0.2 * 5 cm = 1 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror**

 
 
• Produces real and inverted images when the object is placed beyond the focal point.
 
• Produces virtual and magnified images when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirror**
 
 
• Always produces a virtual, erect, and laterally inverted image.
 
• The size of the image is equal to the size of the object.

questions.question: The equivalent resistance of the two resistors of resistance R ohm each connected in series is ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2R ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When resistors are connected in series, their resistances add up.
 
• The total or equivalent resistance (Rₑq) in a series circuit is given by the formula Rₑq = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ.
 
• For two resistors of resistance R ohm each connected in series, the equivalent resistance is R + R.
 
• Thus, the equivalent resistance is 2R ohm.
 
• This is why the correct answer is option 3, which states 2R ohm.

• **Resistors in Parallel**

 
 
• When resistors are connected in parallel, the total resistance decreases.
 
• The formula for the equivalent resistance in a parallel circuit is 1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... + 1/Rₙ.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Combining Series and Parallel Circuits**
 
 
• In complex circuits, series and parallel connections can be combined.
 
• The approach involves simplifying the circuit step by step, first solving series and parallel parts separately.

Total Time = Total Work / Combined Work Rate

questions.question: Which of the following options does NOT represent a property of suspensions?

options.text: The particles of a suspension scatter a beam of light passing through it.
A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
The particles of a suspension cannot be seen by the naked eyes.
A suspension is unstable in nature.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture, meaning its components are not uniformly distributed.
 
• The particles in a suspension are large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
 
• Suspensions are unstable; the particles can settle upon standing.
 
• The particles of a suspension scatter a beam of light passing through it, a phenomenon known as the Tyndall effect.
 
• The correct answer states that the particles of a suspension cannot be seen by the naked eyes, which is incorrect as they can be seen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloids**

 
 
• Colloids are mixtures where the particle size is intermediate between that of a solution and a suspension.
 
• Particles in a colloid are not visible to the naked eye but can scatter light (Tyndall effect).
 
 
 
• **Solutions**
 
 
• Solutions are homogeneous mixtures where the solute is completely dissolved in the solvent.
 
• The particles in a solution are at the molecular or ionic level and do not scatter light.
 
 
 
• **Emulsions**
 
 
• Emulsions are a type of colloid where two immiscible liquids are mixed together.
 
• Common examples include milk and mayonnaise.

questions.question: In which of the following types of reaction is there an exchange of ions between the reactants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a **double displacement reaction**, the ions of two compounds exchange places in an aqueous solution to form two new compounds.
 
• This type of reaction generally occurs between two ionic compounds.
 
• The general formula for a double displacement reaction is AB + CD → AD + CB.
 
• These reactions are often characterized by the formation of a precipitate, a gas, or water.
 
• Double displacement reactions are also known as metathesis reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reaction**

 
 
• In this reaction, a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• It can be represented as AB → A + B.
 
 
 
• **Addition Reaction**
 
 
• Involves two or more substances combining to form a single product.

questions.question: A diver rowing at the speed of 3 km/h in still water takes double the time going 50 km upstream compared to going 50 km downstream. The speed of the diver against the stream is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the distance (50 km) is constant, the speed of the diver is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Time ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 2 : 1 ⇒ Speed ratio (Upstream : Downstream) = 1 : 2

Speed in still water = (Upstream Speed + Downstream Speed) ÷ 2 = (1 + 2) ÷ 2 = 1.5 ratio units.

We are given that still water speed is 3 km/h ⇒ 1.5 ratio units = 3 km/h.

⇒ 1 ratio unit = 2 km/h. Since the upstream speed corresponds to 1 ratio unit, it directly equals 2 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of diver in still water (v) = 3 km/h

Distance traveled upstream and downstream = 50 km

Time taken upstream = 2 × Time taken downstream

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = v − s | Downstream Speed = v + s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48f09262346862c9fff8b21985306db6d9d5a9a92aff7db86ea732a6b26b9e5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = (3 − s) km/h

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = (3 + s) km/h

According to the given condition in the question:

⇒ 50 ÷ (3 − s) = 2 × [50 ÷ (3 + s)]

Canceling 50 from both sides:

⇒ 1 ÷ (3 − s) = 2 ÷ (3 + s)

By cross-multiplying:

⇒ 3 + s = 2 × (3 − s)

⇒ 3 + s = 6 − 2s

⇒ s + 2s = 6 − 3

⇒ 3s = 3

⇒ s = 1 km/h

The speed of the diver against the stream (Upstream Speed):

⇒ U = 3 − s

⇒ U = 3 − 1 = 2 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds. Formula: v = (D + U) ÷ 2, where D is downstream speed and U is upstream speed.

Speed of Stream

It is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds. Formula: s = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Constant Distance Relation

Whenever the distance traveled is constant, the ratio of speeds is always inversely proportional to the ratio of their respective times taken. (Speed ∝ 1 ÷ Time).

questions.question: Which phenomenon causes bending of the ray of light when it moves in the earth's atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmospheric refraction**__.

__
 
• Atmospheric refraction is the bending of light rays as they pass through the Earth's atmosphere, which has varying densities.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because light travels at different speeds in different layers of the atmosphere.
 
• As light moves from one layer to another, it changes direction due to the change in its speed.
 
• Atmospheric refraction is responsible for various optical phenomena such as the twinkling of stars and the apparent position of the sun.
 
• This bending of light also causes the apparent position of celestial objects to shift from their true position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This occurs when particles and molecules in the atmosphere scatter light in different directions.
 
• It is responsible for the blue color of the sky during the day and the red/orange hues during sunrise and sunset.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric reflection**
 
 
• This is the process by which light rays are reflected off the surface of clouds and other atmospheric particles.
 
• It contributes to phenomena such as the visibility of clouds and the brightness of the sky.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric dispersion**
 
 
• This refers to the spreading of light into its component colors due to varying refractive indices for different wavelengths.
 
• It is responsible for the formation of rainbows and the separation of light into a spectrum.

questions.question: Which part of the neuron is responsible for acquiring information?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dendritic tip**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **dendritic tip** is the part of the neuron that is responsible for receiving and acquiring information from other neurons or sensory receptors.
 
• Dendrites are branched extensions of the neuron that conduct electrical signals toward the cell body.
 
• The tips of dendrites have specialized structures known as **synaptic terminals** that facilitate communication with other neurons.
 
• Dendrites play a crucial role in **neural connectivity** and the formation of neural networks.
 
• The structure and branching pattern of dendrites can influence the **strength and integration** of synaptic inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Axon**

 
 
• The axon is a long, slender projection of the neuron that conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body towards other neurons or effectors.
 
• Axons are typically involved in the transmission of information over long distances within the nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Cell Body**
 
 
• The cell body, or soma, contains the nucleus and other organelles essential for the neuron's functions.
 
• It is responsible for maintaining the metabolic activities of the neuron.
 
 
 
• **Synapse**
 
 
• The synapse is the junction between two neurons or between a neuron and a target cell, where communication occurs through neurotransmitter release.
 
• Synaptic transmission is a crucial process for information flow within the nervous system.

questions.question: When an empty bottle is closed air tight and pushed inside water it bounces back when it is released. This is because ________.

options.text: water does not exert force on an empty bottle
gravitational force on a bottle is equal to the buoyant force of the water
upthrust of water on a bottle is greater than the gravitational force acting on the bottle
gravitational force acting on the bottle is greater than the upthrust of water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**upthrust of water on a bottle is greater than the gravitational force acting on the bottle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an empty bottle is pushed underwater, it displaces a volume of water equal to its own volume.
 
• The water exerts an upward buoyant force on the bottle, known as upthrust.
 
• Since the bottle is empty (filled with air), its density is much lower than the density of water.
 
• The upthrust exerted by the water is greater than the gravitational force acting on the empty bottle.
 
• This difference in forces causes the bottle to bounce back to the surface when it is released.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buoyant Force**

 
 
• It is the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object submerged in it.
 
• The magnitude of the buoyant force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
 
 
• **Archimedes' Principle**
 
 
• This principle states that any object submerged in a fluid experiences a buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces.
 
• It explains why objects float or sink in fluids.
 
 
 
• **Density**
 
 
• Density is defined as mass per unit volume of a substance.
 
• Objects with lower density than the fluid they are in will float, while those with higher density will sink.

questions.question: What is the valency of carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The valency of carbon is **four**.
 
• Carbon has **four electrons** in its outer shell.
 
• It needs **four more electrons** to complete its octet, hence its valency is four.
 
• Carbon forms **four covalent bonds** with other atoms to achieve a stable electronic configuration.
 
• Common carbon compounds include **methane (CH₄)**, where carbon forms four single bonds with hydrogen atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon Compounds**

 
 
• Carbon can form a wide variety of compounds due to its ability to form stable covalent bonds with other carbon atoms.
 
• These compounds can be simple molecules like methane or complex structures like proteins and DNA.
 
 
 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**
 
 
• Carbon exists in several allotropes including graphite, diamond, and graphene.
 
• Each allotrope has distinct physical properties due to differences in the arrangement of carbon atoms.
 
 
 
• **Organic Chemistry**
 
 
• The study of carbon compounds is known as organic chemistry.
 
• It encompasses the study of the structure, properties, and reactions of carbon-containing compounds.

questions.question: According to the law of constant proportion, what will be the correct ratio of obtained oxygen and hydrogen (O : H) after decomposition of 18 g water?

__
 
• According to the law of constant proportion, a chemical compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• Water (H₂O) is composed of hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio of 2:16 by mass.
 
• The molar mass of water is 18 g/mol, with oxygen contributing 16 g/mol and hydrogen contributing 2 g/mol.
 
• Upon decomposition of 18 g of water, 16 g of oxygen and 2 g of hydrogen will be obtained.
 
• This ratio of the mass of oxygen to hydrogen (O:H) after decomposition is 16:2, confirming the law of constant proportion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**

 
 
• This law states that if two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass**
 
 
• This law states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
 
 
• **Law of Definite Composition**
 
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains the same elements in the exact same proportions by mass.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms does NOT show asexual reproduction by means of fission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthworm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually and not by asexual means like fission.
 
• Plasmodium, Amoeba, and Leishmania are known to reproduce asexually through fission.
 
• Amoeba reproduces by binary fission, where the organism splits into two equal halves.
 
• Plasmodium reproduces through multiple fission, where one cell divides into many smaller cells.
 
• Leishmania also reproduces through binary fission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• It is a type of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes.
 
• Offspring are genetically identical to the parent organism.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, and spore formation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**
 
 
• This is a form of asexual reproduction common in prokaryotes and some single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• The parent organism divides into two approximately equal parts.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**
 
 
• In multiple fission, the nucleus divides several times before the cell divides into multiple new cells.
 
• This is commonly observed in some protozoa like Plasmodium.

⇒ 1500 = B's cost price × 1.25

⇒ B's cost price = 1500 / 1.25

⇒ B's cost price = ₹1,200

B's cost price = A's selling price

⇒ A's cost price = 1200 / 1.2

• The SI unit of acceleration is meters per second squared (m/s²).
 
• Acceleration can be caused by changing the speed of an object, its direction of motion, or both.

• It is calculated as the displacement per unit of time.

• Distance is a scalar quantity that refers to the total path length covered by an object during its motion.
 
• It does not take the direction of motion into account.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is/are NOT unicellular?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants are **multicellular organisms**, meaning they are composed of multiple cells that work together to perform various functions.
 
• Each plant cell has a specific role, contributing to the overall structure and function of the plant.
 
• Unlike unicellular organisms, plants have specialized cells for different tasks such as photosynthesis, nutrient transport, and reproduction.
 
• Examples of unicellular organisms include Amoeba, Paramoecium, and Chlamydomonas, which are composed of a single cell that performs all the necessary life functions.
 
• Multicellular organisms like plants have a higher level of organization and complexity compared to unicellular organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amoeba**

 
 
• Amoeba are unicellular organisms that move and ingest food using pseudopodia, which are temporary projections of the cell.
 
• They are commonly found in freshwater environments and play a role in nutrient cycling.
 
 
 
• **Paramoecium**
 
 
• Paramoecium are unicellular organisms that use cilia for movement and feeding.
 
• They are often found in aquatic habitats and are known for their slipper-like shape.
 
 
 
• **Chlamydomonas**
 
 
• Chlamydomonas are unicellular green algae that have flagella for movement and are capable of photosynthesis.
 
• They serve as a model organism in biological research due to their simple structure and ease of cultivation.
